section_summary: This section concludes a U.S. Navy report on the condition, internment, and liberation of Spanish Jesuit missionaries and Mercedarian nuns on Saipan following their mistreatment and forced relocation by Japanese authorities. It also contains Despatch No. 3446 from U.S. Ambassador Carlton J. H. Hayes in Madrid transmitting an article from the Spanish newspaper Madrid along with an English translation of significant passages. The transmitted materials highlight the American liberation of the Catholic religious community and Chamorros on Saipan as exceptionally valuable pro-Allied propaganda in Spain and Latin America.

subfiles.about: Concluding pages of a U.S. Navy report detailing the experiences, internment, and liberation of Spanish Jesuit missionaries and Mercedarian nuns on Saipan.
subfiles.from: United States Naval Island Commander of Saipan
subfiles.summary: Saipan report: Father Tardío and Brother Oroquieta arrived at Camp Susupe in July 1944; Japanese seized the Garapan church in 1940, banned rites in December 1941, and moved clergy and Chamorros into hills; they recovered under American care.
subfiles.title: Report from the United States Naval Island Commander of Saipan on the Religious Community on the Island

subfiles.about: Despatch from U.S. Ambassador Carlton J. H. Hayes transmitting a Spanish newspaper article and English translation regarding the American liberation of Spanish Catholic missionaries on Saipan.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Carlton J. H. Hayes transmits an article published in the Madrid evening newspaper Madrid on November 13, 1944, along with an English translation of key paragraphs detailing the liberation of Spanish Mercedarian missionaries on Saipan by American forces. The article reviews the establishment of the Mercedarian mission in 1928 by Mother Margarita María Maturana, recounts Japanese wartime suppression and internment leading to the death of one nun, and contrasts Japanese oppression with the benevolent assistance and religious freedom provided by U.S. forces. Hayes emphasizes the extraordinary propaganda value of these unsolicited Spanish testimonials for audiences in Spain and notes their transmission by United Press to Buenos Aires for wider distribution throughout Latin America.
subfiles.title: Valuable Propaganda from Publicity on Liberation of Catholic Religious Community on Island of Saipan
